source_title: Updated Russia, Ukraine begin ceasefire in city of Oleshky as deadly strikes continue elsewhere News - World | 13 minutes ago
source_excerpt:
Russian-occupied Oleshky, hollowed out since 2022, is site of war's 1st significant ceasefire
Russia and Ukraine began a regional ceasefire to allow the start of a humanitarian effort in the Russian-occupied town of ‌Oleshky, both sides said Tuesday, but also engaged in strikes elsewhere, including the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv.
The ceasefire, which is expected to proceed through Sunday, should enable deliveries of aid, as well as evacuations from the front-line town in southern Ukraine that is grappling with acute shortages of food and medicine.
The head of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's ruling faction in parliament, David Arakhamia, called it the "biggest de-escalation since 2022." Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February of that year, ceasefires have been relegated to occasional holiday periods.

On Telegram, Russia's Defence Ministry said it stopped shelling in the direction of ​Kherson from 4 a.m. Moscow time, to prepare for the ⁠effort in Oleshky.
Oleshky lies on the eastern bank of the Dnipro River in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, opposite the city of Kherson, which is held by Ukrainian forces. Russian troops seized Oleshky during the first days of their February 2022 invasion and have controlled it ever since.

Oleshky has suffered extensive war damage and was hit hard by flooding after the destruction of the nearby Kakhovka Dam in 2023. The United States has said only a few thousand people remain in Oleshky, from a prewar population of 24,000.
Residents and officials have reported severe shortages of food, medicine and other basic supplies.
Kyiv residents said they hoped the Oleshky ceasefire would finally bring some relief to locals, but optimism was tinged with concerns that Russia would not abide by the terms of the agreement.
"I want to hope that things will indeed work out this way, that the agreement will actually be implemented, and that the Russian side will keep its word," Olha Haiduk, 59, told Reuters.
One resident who managed to flee Oleshky told Reuters many of those remaining there are sick or elderly, and that it would be difficult for them to relocate.
A still image taken from an undated drone video released Sept. 12 shows destroyed buildings in Oleshky, a Russian-occupied city in Ukraine's southern Kherson region. (34th Separate Marine Brigade Borysfen/Reuters)
Oleshky has suffered extensive war damage and was hit hard by flooding after the destruction of the nearby Kakhovka Dam in 2023. The United States has said only a few thousand people remain in Oleshky, from a prewar population of 24,000.
Residents and officials have reported severe shortages of food, medicine and other basic supplies.
As the regional ceasefire proceeded, new strikes on Tuesday hit the Southern Bridge and subway infrastructure in Kyiv, forcing a suspension of traffic, city officials said, while a Reuters witness ⁠heard explosions.
Russia's ‌overnight attacks included 16 ballistic missiles and ​more than 280 ​drones, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday, ​calling it a ⁠serious ⁠escalation ‌against Ukrainian logistics.
"Tragically, there have been casualties and hits in Kyiv, including ⁠on the South Bridge," he said on ‌X, referring to one of the main road bridges over the ​Dnipro River that ⁠bisects the Ukrainian capital.
Ukrainian rescuers clear fallen trees near a destroyed car on a road in Kyiv on Tuesday, following a Russian missile strike. (Genya Savilov/AFP/Getty Images)
On ⁠the ⁠Telegram messaging app, the Russian Defence Ministry said ​it has hit transport infrastructure in Kyiv, a logistics hub in the Kharkiv region as well as industrial facilities ​and cargo vessels elsewhere it cited ⁠as being put to military use.
Russia has significantly stepped up its strikes on logistics in and around Kyiv in recent months, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Telegram, and the city's defence council discussed a "project to build combined water crossings over the River Dnipro and the access roads leading to them."
In Russia, a drone attack killed one person in the western city of Bryansk near the border with Ukraine, authorities said.
Another person was killed and 30 injured as a drone hit a bus in the Russian-controlled part of Ukraine's southeastern region of Zaporizhzhia, local officials said.
Reuters could not immediately independently verify the reports. Russia and ⁠Ukraine deny deliberately targeting civilians.
Finnish, Norwegian leaders speak to Putin
White House envoys have talked to both sides in recent days to try and find a solution as the U.S. looks to mediate a peace deal to end the war, Europe's deadliest conflict since the Second World War. But questions have emerged as to American loyalties in the wake of a diesel deal the U.S. struck with Russia, and antagonistic statements made by U.S. President Donald Trump regarding Zelenskyy.
On Friday, Zelenskyy said peace negotiators from ​Ukraine, Russia and the United States had agreed to meet at a technical level in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi to continue ⁠the talks.

Meanwhile, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere on Tuesday held a phone ‌call with Russian President Vladimir Putin regarding the war in Ukraine, Stubb's office said in a statement.
"The discussion was ​frank and substantive. We are neighbouring countries ⁠to Russia. ⁠The outcome of ‌this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions," Stubb ⁠said in a statement.
Western European leaders ​have mostly shunned contact with Putin ​since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine. Russia has frequently accused European governments of stoking the war by arming Ukraine and refusing ‌to talk to Moscow.
An aide for Zelenskyy confirmed he was briefed by the Finnish and Norwegian leaders after their call with Putin.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told the Interfax news agency that the two Nordic leaders offered nothing new ⁠on the Ukraine ⁠conflict, adding ⁠that ​European countries were simply ​seeking ⁠a role in the negotiation process.

रूस और यूक्रेन ने मंगलवार को रूस के कब्जे वाले दक्षिणी यूक्रेन के ओलेश्की शहर में मानवीय प्रयासों की अनुमति देने के लिए एक क्षेत्रीय युद्धविराम शुरू किया। दोनों पक्षों ने कहा कि यह समझौता रविवार तक चलने की उम्मीद है, जिसका उद्देश्य भोजन और दवा की आपूर्ति के साथ-साथ शेष नागरिकों के लिए निकासी को सक्षम बनाना है।

राष्ट्रपति वोलोडिमिर ज़ेलेंस्की के सत्तारूढ़ गुट के प्रमुख डेविड अराखमिया ने इसे 2022 के बाद से सबसे बड़ा तनाव कम करने वाला कदम बताया। रूस के रक्षा मंत्रालय ने टेलीग्राम पर, मॉस्को समयानुसार सुबह 4 बजे से खेरसॉन की दिशा में गोलाबारी रोकने की घोषणा की।

## ओलेश्की में मानवीय स्थिति

ओलेश्की को 2023 में कखोव्का बांध के नष्ट होने के बाद गंभीर युद्ध क्षति और बाढ़ का सामना करना पड़ा है। अमेरिकी अनुमानों के अनुसार, युद्ध से पहले की 24,000 की आबादी में से अब केवल कुछ हजार लोग वहां बचे हैं।

जबकि कीव के नागरिकों ने उम्मीद जताई कि ओलेश्की समझौते से राहत मिलेगी, कुछ लोगों ने इस बात पर संदेह व्यक्त किया कि रूसी सेना समझौते का पालन करेगी या नहीं। रॉयटर्स तुरंत सभी परिचालन विवरणों की स्वतंत्र रूप से पुष्टि नहीं कर सका।

## जारी हमले और हताहत

ओलेश्की में क्षेत्रीय युद्धविराम के बावजूद, मंगलवार को अन्य क्षेत्रों में संघर्ष और हमले जारी रहे:

* **कीव बुनियादी ढांचा:** शहर के अधिकारियों ने बताया कि दक्षिणी पुल और मेट्रो बुनियादी ढांचे पर हमले हुए, जिससे यातायात बाधित हुआ और विस्फोटों की आवाज सुनी गई। राष्ट्रपति ज़ेलेंस्की ने कहा कि रात भर हुए हमलों में 16 बैलिस्टिक मिसाइलें और 280 से अधिक ड्रोन शामिल थे।
* **अन्य स्थानों पर रूसी हमले:** रूस के रक्षा मंत्रालय ने कीव में परिवहन बुनियादी ढांचे, खार्किव क्षेत्र में एक लॉजिस्टिक हब और औद्योगिक सुविधाओं पर हमले की बात कही। मेयर विटाली क्लिट्सको ने हाल के महीनों में लॉजिस्टिक्स पर हमलों में तेजी आने का उल्लेख किया।
* **सीमावर्ती क्षेत्र:** अधिकारियों ने बताया कि रूस के ब्रायंस्क में एक ड्रोन हमले में एक व्यक्ति की मौत हो गई। ज़ापोरिझिया के रूसी-नियंत्रित हिस्से में, स्थानीय अधिकारियों ने कहा कि एक ड्रोन बस से टकरा गया, जिससे एक व्यक्ति की मौत हो गई और 30 घायल हो गए।

रूस और यूक्रेन दोनों नागरिकों को जानबूझकर निशाना बनाने से इनकार करते हैं। रॉयटर्स हताहतों की संख्या की स्वतंत्र रूप से पुष्टि नहीं कर सका।

## कूटनीतिक विकास

सैन्य संघर्ष के साथ-साथ अंतरराष्ट्रीय कूटनीतिक प्रयास भी जारी रहे। फिनलैंड के राष्ट्रपति अलेक्जेंडर स्टुब और नॉर्वे के प्रधानमंत्री जोनास गहर स्टोर ने युद्ध पर चर्चा करने के लिए रूसी राष्ट्रपति व्लादिमीर पुतिन के साथ फोन पर बातचीत की। राष्ट्रपति ज़ेलेंस्की के एक सहायक ने पुष्टि की कि कॉल के बाद यूक्रेनी नेतृत्व को जानकारी दी गई थी। इस बीच, यूक्रेन, रूस और संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका से जुड़े तकनीकी स्तर की शांति वार्ता नवंबर के पहले पतन में अबू धाबी में निर्धारित है।

## व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ और सत्यापन

* **आधिकारिक बयानों की जाँच करें:** आधिकारिक यूक्रेनी और रूसी मंत्रालय के अपडेट या स्थापित अंतरराष्ट्रीय निरीक्षकों के माध्यम से मानवीय गलियारे की स्थिति की पुष्टि करें।
* **यात्रा सलाह की निगरानी करें:** प्रभावित क्षेत्रीय क्षेत्रों में पारगमन सुरक्षा का आकलन करने से पहले आधिकारिक सरकारी अपडेट की जाँच करें।
* **रिपोर्टों का सत्यापन करें:** स्वतंत्र समाचार संगठनों और सत्यापन योग्य निगरानी समूहों के साथ हताहतों और हमलों के दावों की क्रॉस-समीक्षा करें।

en_body:
Russia and Ukraine began a regional ceasefire on Tuesday to allow humanitarian efforts in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, located in southern Ukraine's Kherson region. Both sides stated the agreement is expected to proceed through Sunday, aiming to enable food and medicine deliveries alongside evacuations for remaining residents.

David Arakhamia, the head of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's ruling faction in parliament, described the arrangement as the largest de-escalation since 2022. Russia's Defence Ministry stated on Telegram that it halted shelling in the direction of Kherson starting at 4 a.m. Moscow time.

## Humanitarian Situation in Oleshky

Oleshky has experienced severe war damage and flooding following the 2023 destruction of the nearby Kakhovka Dam. U.S. estimates indicate only a few thousand people remain out of a prewar population of 24,000. Residents and officials reported acute shortages of food, medicine, and basic supplies.

While Kyiv residents expressed hope that the Oleshky agreement would offer relief, some voiced skepticism regarding whether Russian forces would adhere to its terms. Reuters could not immediately independently verify all operational details.

## Ongoing Strikes and Casualties

Despite the regional ceasefire in Oleshky, fighting and strikes continued in other areas on Tuesday:

* **Kyiv Infrastructure:** City officials reported strikes hitting the Southern Bridge and subway infrastructure, suspending traffic and prompting explosions reported by witnesses. President Zelenskyy stated that overnight attacks included 16 ballistic missiles and over 280 drones.
* **Russian Strikes Elsewhere:** Russia's Defence Ministry reported hitting transport infrastructure in Kyiv, a logistics hub in the Kharkiv region, and industrial facilities. Mayor Vitali Klitschko noted stepped-up strikes on logistics in recent months.
* **Border Regions:** Authorities reported one person killed in a drone attack in Bryansk, Russia. In Russian-controlled parts of Zaporizhzhia, local officials stated a drone hit a bus, killing one person and injuring 30.

Neither side denies the strikes, though both Russia and Ukraine deny deliberately targeting civilians. Reuters could not independently verify casualty figures.

## Diplomatic Developments

International diplomatic efforts continued alongside the military conflict. Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss the war. An aide to President Zelenskyy confirmed that Ukrainian leadership was briefed following the call. Meanwhile, planned technical-level peace talks involving Ukraine, Russia, and the United States are scheduled for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi.

## Practical Implications and Verification

* **Check Official Statements:** Verify humanitarian corridor statuses through official Ukrainian and Russian ministerial updates or established international monitors.
* **Monitor Travel Advisories:** Check official government updates before assessing transit security in affected regional zones.
* **Verify Reports:** Cross-reference breaking casualty and strike claims with independent news organizations and verifiable monitoring groups.
